headline: Data Centers Pay Fair Grid Share
short_summary: This bill aims to ensure large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of their grid infrastructure costs, potentially reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Senator Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (with amendments).
news_headline: Lawmakers OK Governor's Tweaks to Energy Cost Shift Bills
news_summary: Governor Spanberger approved amendments to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to shift energy distribution and capacity costs onto high-load users like data centers and large manufacturers. The changes allow the State Corporation Commission to determine fair share contributions, potentially saving residential customers about $5.52 monthly.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This legislation mandates that data centers report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for potential future water management policies.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential future regulation).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency regarding data centers' water consumption, which has been a top complaint against the industry.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill grants localities more authority to regulate the placement and noise levels of data centers, addressing community concerns about development impact.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, local governments, Delegate Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Sterling Resident Reports Excessive Noise, Pollution from Data Center
news_summary: A Sterling resident reported excessive noise and fumes from a data center's backup generators running for nearly 24 hours, exceeding local noise limits. This incident highlights ongoing community concerns about data center noise and pollution, which HB 153 aims to address through siting and noise regulations.
